item.title: The People We Love Are Only on Loan
item.description:
Grief

The People We Love Are Only on Loan

What the Stoics knew about grief and loss.

Posted August 18, 2026

Key points
  • A life need not be long to be sufficient; a short life may be complete.
  • Death is a loss to the living, but not necessarily a misfortune to the dead.
  • Treat the people you love as precious loans from fortune, not permanent possessions.
The Angel Standing in the Sun, by JMW Turner (cropped)
Source: WIkimedia Commons/JMW Turner/Public domain

The Stoic Seneca (d. 65 CE) was the master of the "consolation," a letter written for the express purpose of comforting someone who has been bereaved. Seneca wrote at least three consolations, to Marcia, to Polybius, and to Helvia. In the Consolation to Helvia, he comforts his own mother on "losing" him to exile—an unusual case, and literary innovation, of the lamented consoling the lamenter.

The emperor Marcus Aurelius (d. 180 CE) had at least 14 children with his wife Faustina, but only four daughters and one unfortunate son, Commodus, outlived their parents. In the Meditations, Marcus likens his children to leaves, and paraphrases Homer in the Iliad:

Men come and go as leaves year by year upon the trees. Those of autumn the wind sheds upon the ground, but when the spring returns the forest buds forth with fresh vines.

The image is deliberately impersonal. To a parent, the death of a child is a profound loss; but to nature, it is no more extraordinary than the falling of a leaf. The Stoic challenge is, somehow, to hold both perspectives at once.

Marcus was a Stoic, and would have known, at least in principle, how to cope with grief, loss, and bereavement. But if Seneca could have consoled Marcus on the loss of his children, and could only have told him three things, what might he have told him?

1. A Life Can Be Sufficient

First, Marcus, remember that life is given to us with death as a precondition. Some people die sooner than others, but life, on a cosmic scale, is so short that, really, it makes no difference. Even children are known to die—indeed, they often do—and these, Marcus, simply happened to be your own. A human life, however long or short, or great or small, is of little historical and no cosmic consequence. Since a life can never be long or great enough, the most that it can be is sufficient, and we would do better to concentrate on what that might mean. A short life may be complete, just as a long life may be squandered, or drag on for far too long. It is not how many years we have, but what we make of those years, or the shape of those years.

2. Is Death Really Such an Evil?

Second, it may be that death is in fact preferable to life. Life is full of suffering, and grieving only adds to it, whereas death is the permanent release from every possible pain. Indeed, many people who have died—think only of our friend Cicero—would have died happier if they had died sooner. If we do not pity the unborn, why should we pity the dead, who at least had the benefit, if benefit it is, of having existed? The unborn cry out as soon as they are delivered into the world, but to the dead we never have to block our ears. If weep we must, it is not over death, but the whole of life, that we should weep. Marcus, you may find this bleak, or me brutal. But if death is a loss to those who remain, it does not follow that it is a misfortune to the departed—and we should not deepen our grief by assuming it is so. When King Midas compelled the wise Silenus to reveal what was best for human beings, he replied: "Not to be born; and, failing that, to die soon."

article continues after advertisement

3. The People We Love Are Only on Loan

Third, we should treat the people we love not as permanent possessions but as temporary loans from fortune. When, in the evening, you kiss your wife and children goodnight, reflect on the possibility that they, and you, might never wake up. In the morning when you kiss them goodbye, reflect on the possibility that they, or you, might never come home. That way you’ll be better prepared for their eventual loss, and, what’s more, savour and sublime whatever time you spend with them—and, in that way, lead them to love you more.

If you do lose a loved one, do not grieve, or no more than is appropriate, or no more than they would have wanted you to, but be grateful for the moments that you shared, and consider how much poorer your life would have been if they had never entered into it.

Sometimes, like now, Marcus, our grieving is recent or prominent, but in truth we are permanently grieving. We accumulate losses—people, places, possibilities, former selves. Much of that grief simply recedes, only to resurface more softly in our quieter moments.

Everything leaves us, and if they do not, we leave them.

item.title: The Need to Stop Food Noise
item.description:
Appetite

The Need to Stop Food Noise

Food noise can disrupt our relationship with food in a multitude of ways.

Posted August 18, 2026

Key points
  • The use of GLP-1 and GIP weight-loss drugs has revealed the profound affect of food noise.
  • Research into those drugs has pointed to complex food noise mechanisms.
  • Information about food noise could benefit many who struggle with their weight.
Source: Wildpixel / iStock

The advent of the GLP-1 and GIP agonist drugs has brought along with it an increased focus on “food noise.” Many people on one or both of those medications report a serious reduction in food noise, which has been defined as “intrusive and often unwanted thoughts about food.” As more and more research has emerged, reduction of food noise has been identified as a major key to the weight loss seen with these drugs, and to weight loss in general.

The Science

In people with type 2 diabetes, the GLP-1s and GIPs (known as incretin hormones) have been shown to improve glycemic control and reduce plasma glucose. As it turns out, both type 2 diabetics and people with obesity show impaired GLP-1 secretion in the gut. Both groups taking the supplemental incretin hormones show a reduction in food intake and appetite.

GLP-1 and GIP supplements have a wide distribution in many areas of the brain as well, thanks to their ability to cross the blood-brain barrier via the paraventricular organs. Most notably, they can affect the hypothalamus, which is like an orchestra leader for many feedback mechanisms related to appetite and appetite control. For example, introducing incretin hormones to the hypothalamus has been shown to reduce hedonic eating, which is eating for pleasure rather than hunger.

Other areas of the brain that are affected by the supplemental incretin hormones include the parietal cortex, the brainstem, and the dopaminergic system. The dopaminergic system is a particular area of interest. Research has shown that people with higher body mass index (BMI) show altered dopamine D2 receptor density, which can dampen the experience of food and turn up the volume on food noise.

The Human Aspect

All this complexity means that mitigating food noise can show up in many ways. The response can be quite individual. Case in point: Emotional eating is the nemesis of many individuals who are trying to lose weight or prevent weight gain. Some people are more prone to trying to regulate mood by eating than others. Different people will also have different emotional responses to food, based on many variables including culture, family, and environment. In addition, an individual food may or may not trigger an emotional response depending on visual appeal, high caloric density, or even convenience.

article continues after advertisement

People respond to the food they see, or food cues, differently. Research has found that sometimes being in a loud, busy environment can drown out internal cues and cause people to overeat. And, of course, there is our ever-enticing environment with the abundance of convenience foods and appealing visual cues on media.

But food cues need not be present. Research has found that people can think about food in its absence as well.

Now, there is a plethora of self-report questionnaires to evaluate the different aspects of food noise. To name a few: power of food, eating in the absence of hunger, cravings scale, food cue sensitivity, negative affect, fatigue/boredom, lack of control over eating, lack of satiation, and food cue rumination. All of these are designed as assessment tools, but it’s not clear how widely they are used.

Keeping It Simple

It is worth getting the message out about food noise. In a distinctly limited and unofficial poll I conducted, I did not run into anyone who had heard of food noise or knew what it is, including some who are on a GLP-1. It may be well known to health writers, researchers, and others in the health field, so it may seem to those folks that it is part of the general zeitgeist. However, that is probably not the case.

article continues after advertisement

Some individuals on the incretin drugs report that they had been unaware of the food noise that was part of their everyday existence. Because it was always there, it went unnoticed until it wasn’t there.

One of the huge advantages of learning about food noise is that it can take away the guilt, the low self-esteem, and the frustration experienced by many who deem themselves lacking in willpower or a hopeless case. To keep it simple, weight loss coaches or health professionals can explain that our bodies and brains can become hijacked, causing us to lose track of what a healthy approach to food consumption looks like and feels like.

It can also be used as a way to explain why dieting can be a recipe for failure. Food noise gets turned up when the body is in restriction, making it very difficult to sustain. This can lead to a never-ending cycle of yo-yo dieting. This speaks to the so-called “chronic nature of obesity.”

Unfortunately, GLP-1s and GIPs do not permanently alter the complexity that is food noise. It comes back if there is cessation of these drugs. Our bodies and brains do not start to take over and reinvent themselves in ways that would allow us to carry on with appetite control on our own.

All things considered, the more we can create awareness around food noise, the better. It can be a useful step toward self-awareness for anyone who deals with how to eat, whether they are actively trying to lose weight or just trying to skip the potato chips they normally have with lunch.
